sources.excerpt: PostHog ingests and stores your analytics, errors, replays, and business data so you and your agents can query and act on it. Join 500,000+ teams already shipping with PostHog.

CARLES SALVADOR — page shows 'James Hawkins' and 'Co-CEO' with bio: 'I spent the first 10 years of my career trying to be a professional cyclist... I started working with Tim on a few ideas... We built PostHog during the Y Combinator W20 batch, and launched in February 2020.'

draft:
Hi James,

I came across PostHog and your work as Co-CEO.

I’m exploring Product Gym: Product Gym is a concept being validated: codebase-informed hands-on practice environments where customers learn to use software by doing, with behavioral telemetry to reveal which workflows they master or struggle with.

I’m reaching out for customer interviews and would value your perspective on People responsible for helping customers understand, adopt and use a complex software product.. I’m still validating whether this is useful.

Would you be open to a 15-minute conversation about how customers learn newly released features?

Funding stage information is not available on the website. While the GitHub repo confirms open-source status, specific funding rounds or investor information would require external sources (e.g., Crunchbase, PitchBook).

The task instructed to gather ALL clearly matching companies from the source, but PostHog's site only covers their own product. No comparable B2B open-source product analytics companies (e.g., Amplitude, Mixpanel, Heap, TelemetryDeck, or others) are listed or linked within this domain.

None of the 6 companies listed are explicitly described as open-source in the article, unlike PostHog which is emphasized as open-source. The criteria mentions 'B2B open-source product analytics software platforms' — none of these alternatives are open-source.
The article does not provide funding stage information for any of the 6 companies (Mixpanel, Amplitude, Fullstory, Heap, Google Analytics, LogRocket), so stage cannot be determined from this source.

Google Analytics (GA4) is primarily a web analytics and marketing attribution tool rather than a dedicated product analytics platform, making it a less direct comparison to PostHog than the other 5 companies.

Fullstory and LogRocket lean more toward qualitative insights, session replay, and debugging than comprehensive product analytics, making them partial fits compared to PostHog's quantitative and developer-focused approach.

The company list on technologychecker.io is sorted by LinkedIn following (largest organizations first), but the task criteria specify Developer tools companies. Most listed companies are NOT in Software Development or Developer tools category - they are healthcare, retail, banking, education, government, etc. Only ~10 of 50 companies listed are in Software Development or Technology, Information and Internet categories.

Many PostHog detections occur on non-core subdomains (careers sites, conference sites, documentation portals, trust/compliance pages, course catalogs) rather than on primary product domains. These may not represent the companies' core product analytics needs.

The page explicitly states: 'a detection may be one storefront rather than a company-wide deployment' - meaning PostHog usage detected does not necessarily indicate a B2B open-source product analytics platform deployment on their main product.

Funding stages are listed as 'Public Company', 'Privately Held', 'Self-Owned', 'Government Agency', 'Educational', 'Nonprofit' rather than traditional VC funding stages (Seed, Series A, etc.). The ICP allows 'Any' funding stage, so this does not disqualify any company.
Agencies and consulting businesses are explicitly excluded per ICP. Virtusa Corporation (IT Services and IT Consulting) is a consulting business and should be excluded.

The page contains 50 visible companies total. Of these, only PostHog itself, HubSpot, MongoDB, Railway, Veeam, Xero, Cvent (Software Development companies) and Outlier AI, Varsity Tutors, Nova Talent (Technology/Internet) clearly fit the B2B Developer tools / Product Analytics ICP. The remaining 35+ companies are healthcare, retail, banking, education, government, defense, manufacturing - none match the 'B2B open-source product analytics software platforms' criterion.

No pagination or 'show more' beyond the 50 visible companies is available without login. The site mentions 139,813 total domains but only 75,665 matched to company records. Cannot access the full dataset without authentication.
